$comment: The application patterns the overview names in §8, one row each; check-data.mjs fails when the count differs. The specification names the patterns without specifying them, so plain is a one-sentence reading of each name. channelChoice is the site's reading of §8's first paragraph.

patterns.name: Remote contract call through proxy contracts
patterns.plain: A contract on one ledger calls a contract on another through proxy contracts, and the result comes back later as the reply.

patterns.name: Escrow, mint, then burn
patterns.plain: Escrow, mint, then burn, as steps on different ledgers whose outcomes arrive later as replies.

patterns.name: Two-phase commit across ledgers
patterns.plain: A change that several ledgers commit together, coordinated through messages whose outcomes arrive later as replies.

channelChoice.plain: Applications are asynchronous: a send returns before the destination executes, and the outcome arrives later as a reply. When several channels connect the same two ledgers, for example with verifiers that accept different finality, the application chooses one at send time. Lower finality gives lower latency and a risk of reorganization. The recommended level is final or safe state; a channel whose verifier accepts anything earlier is used at its users' own risk.
